Definition: to squeeze out juice; figuratively, to trample
BiblicalUsage: This verb for treading down — pressing, crushing underfoot — occurs once, in Malachi 4:3: 'And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do this, saith the LORD of hosts.' It is the last promise of the Old Testament's last prophet.
TheologicalSignificance: The Old Testament ends with the righteous treading the wicked to ashes — a hard promise, and a just one — and I believe it is the hope of everyone who has watched the wicked prosper.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
